new: ; Runtime Arabic shaping for typed text (names, nicknames, box names, mail).
; The tables come from gen_arabic_input.py, which builds them from the same
; letter table as the build-time shaper and checks that ShapeArabicName gives
; the same bytes as pc_arabic.shape(text, ligatures=False).
; Give each Arabic letter of the "@"-terminated string at hl the form its
; neighbours call for, in place, in logical order. A letter may come in any of
; its forms (the keyboard types isolated ones), so shaping again changes
; nothing. Joining never crosses a character that is not a letter: a space,
; digits, punctuation, "<NEXT>", the entry field's lines. No lam-alef ligature.
ld c, 0 ; ARABIC_FORM_FINAL if the previous character joins this one

; the next letter joins this one if this one is dual-joining
; Return a = the letter (row of ArabicForms) of glyph a, or carry if glyph a
; is not an Arabic letter. Preserves bc, de and hl.

new: ; Right-to-left text for the Arabic translation (see RTL_*_F).
; Text placed at explicit coordinates is drawn left to right, as the English
; was, by the outermost PlaceString (or DoTextUntilTerminator), which owns the
; line; when the line ends its tiles are reversed in place, so it reads right
; to left inside the same footprint. Text printed into the speech box is drawn
; leftward from the box's right inner edge instead, so it is typed from the
; right and its lines end on the left. Digits always read left to right
; Own the line that starts at hl.
; A new line starts at hl.
; The owner's string ended at bc: reverse its last line and give the line up.
; The line ends at hl. Preserves bc, de and hl.
; Numerals drawn leftward ended right of hl: put them back left to right.
; hl = where the speech box's first line starts
; hl = where the speech box's second line starts
; Place string de right to left with its lines ending at hl (their right edge).
; Like PlaceString, returns bc = the pen (left of the last line).
; rst PlaceString for a text command; leftward in the speech box.
